reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Regal Coin and BitConnect lending programs, directs viewers to join through a link, and encourages putting money into them. The speaker presents daily interest and passive income, along with a lending-wallet transaction page, as ways to make money. Although a research disclaimer and advice to start small are included, the explicit investment promotion remains.

opening.argument: The speaker expressly presents this as personal commentary rather than professional financial advice: he says, "I'm not a financial advisor" and asks viewers to conduct their own research. He also admits he has been involved only a few months and "don't know everything," which is uncertainty rather than a guarantee. The presentation further identifies technical issues with Regal Coin and tells viewers to start small. Those qualifications make the material a personal, risk-aware discussion of crypto participation, not a deceptive certification that returns are assured.

That's the way you want to do it. You want to start out small.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited invitations show enthusiasm and a referral appeal, but they do not establish that the speaker concealed uncertainty or guaranteed an outcome. The same presentation openly says he is not an advisor, directs viewers to research independently, reports technical issues, and recommends starting small. The reported interest is explicitly presented as his own experience, not as independently verified proof.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not erase the concrete solicitation. Immediately alongside the disclaimer, the speaker asks viewers to join his team, put money into the programs, and make money. His statement that he is getting interest every day and calling the result passive income supplies the promotional message; saying viewers should research does not substantiate those earnings claims.

opening.argument: The video's main instructional material teaches cryptocurrency security and operational hygiene. It recommends difficult passwords, VPN use, two-factor authorization, recovery email protection, separate hardware, alternative operating systems, and avoiding public Wi-Fi for wallets and exchanges. The speaker also explains that he is sharing his own experiences and invites questions so viewers can learn. A discussion that includes a demonstration of an account interface and practical security guidance is better understood as crypto education and commentary than as a standalone solicitation.

citations.quote: I want to share my experiences in crypto land and I want to learn from you
security you have to have if you're going to get into crypto you have to invest your time in looking into security
two factor authorization. Make sure you use two factor authorization
don't use public Wi-Fi for anything crypto, especially wallets and exchanges.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Security instruction is real, but it does not change the separate portion where the speaker names two programs, directs viewers to join, and links participation to making money. A tutorial can still contain a promotional solicitation; the instructional slides do not explain or substantiate the programs' returns.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The security advice is peripheral to the financial pitch and cannot establish that the promoted programs are ordinary educational examples. The speaker specifically urges viewers to fund them, says he receives interest every day, and labels the result passive income. The account image is only a displayed interface; it does not verify the claimed earnings or explain how they are generated.

opening.argument: The observable commercial feature is a referral-style promotion for named cryptocurrency programs, not proof of a concealed scam mechanism. The description supplies a referral URL, and the slides say to join the team and use the links below. But the material does not show a credential request, a required recruitment payment, or a guaranteed return. The displayed BitConnect screen is an account transaction-detail interface, while the speaker describes his own balance and experience. That supports treating this as ordinary referral commerce or an investment-related promotion without certifying the external service as safe.

citations.quote: REGAL COIN TEAM https://regalcoin.co/ref/WHYN0T10
Here's my Bic Connect. Same thing. You know, $78 in my lending wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the link a referral does not make the promotion ordinary commerce when viewers are told to deposit money into lending programs and are promised an attractive money-making opportunity. The supplied material expressly uses the language of daily interest and passive income. Whether or not credentials are requested, the financial solicitation itself is the relevant conduct.

citations.quote: throw ten dollars in there throw a hundred dollars in there
I'm getting interest every day.
It's passive income

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a credential request does not resolve the central issue. The speaker promotes lending programs, asks viewers to put money into them, invites them to join his team, and connects participation with making money. The referral URL and displayed lending-wallet page reinforce promotion; they do not demonstrate a legitimate ordinary product or independently verify the reported returns.
